name: Seagrass Meadows
genZNote: Seagrass is the one true flowering plant that fully moved into the ocean — not algae, not coral, an actual plant with roots, living entirely underwater.

sections.heading: 🌱 What Seagrass Is
bullets: True flowering plants (not algae or seaweed) that grow fully submerged in shallow coastal waters, rooted in sand or mud.
Form dense underwater meadows in sheltered bays, lagoons and shallow coastal shelves worldwide, from the tropics to temperate coasts.

sections.heading: 🐠 Why Seagrass Matters
bullets: Provide nursery habitat for juvenile fish, shrimp and other species, similar in role to mangroves but in fully submerged shallow water.
Stabilise seafloor sediment with their root systems, reducing coastal erosion.
Store carbon efficiently in their root systems and the sediment beneath them — another major 'blue carbon' ecosystem alongside mangroves.
Support globally significant grazers, most famously dugongs and sea turtles, which feed directly on seagrass.

sections.heading: ⚠️ Threats
bullets: Sensitive to reduced light from water pollution and sediment runoff, since they need sunlight to photosynthesize like any plant.
Damaged by coastal development, dredging, and boat-anchor damage.
Global seagrass cover has declined significantly over past decades, making it one of the least visible but most threatened coastal ecosystems.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Seagrass meadows are underwater flowering plants that stabilise sediment, store blue carbon, and provide nursery habitat and food for species like dugongs and turtles.
keyFacts: True flowering plants, not algae — grow rooted underwater.
Provide nursery habitat and stabilise coastal sediment.
A major 'blue carbon' ecosystem alongside mangroves.
Key food source for dugongs and sea turtles.
commonConfusion: Seagrass is a true plant (with roots and flowers); seaweed/algae are not plants in the same botanical sense — don't conflate the two.

highYieldFacts: Seagrass = true flowering plant, fully submerged.
Primary food source for dugongs and sea turtles.
commonTraps: Don't call seagrass 'seaweed' — seaweed is algae, seagrass is a flowering plant with true roots.
mustRemember: Seagrass = underwater plant meadows; blue carbon storage; dugong/turtle food source.
